effect: Installs an official while the chamber is empty, and calls the emptiness a recess.
available_to: A president, a Senate that has left town, and a vacancy that has been waiting for a vote.
counter: Pro forma sessions. A gavel every few days means the Senate is never in recess, and the appointment never happens.

confused_with.tell: The cronycle installs friends with the chamber's consent; the recessure installs them without it.

senses: The recess appointment: a constitutional power to fill a vacancy while the Senate is out of session, good only until the end of the next session - a temporary official holding a permanent-looking title.

It works because recess is a word the Senate can disprove by showing up. The power is real but the trigger is procedural, so the fight is never about the nominee's qualifications; it is about whether anyone is standing in the chamber to object.
example: *"The nominee had been stalled for eight months, so the **recessure** happened on a Tuesday when the Senate was technically out of town, and the oath was administered by Thursday."*
